purpose: Source-qualified external benchmark and standards anchors for cross-vendor comparison. The register records reported claims and validity limitations; it contains no Luminous candidate results.

status_vocabulary.provider_or_paper_reported: Claim/result reported by the named organization or authors; not independently reproduced by Luminous.
status_vocabulary.independent_benchmark_review: External evaluator's methodology assessment; does not automatically apply to later benchmark revisions.
status_vocabulary.normative_standard: Published standard or Recommendation; not a performance score.
status_vocabulary.field_demonstration: Physical system field result under the exact published workload, site and measurement boundary.
status_vocabulary.active_leaderboard_snapshot: Time-sensitive leaderboard snapshot, including model + harness configuration; recheck before use.

entries.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
methodology_facts: Agentic audits, expert adjudication and blind re-implementation were used to repair or retire 480 of 731 tasks.
Hardened protocol restricts network access to the model endpoint and re-grades patches in a clean container.
limitations: Results are paper-reported; no independent Luminous replication.
The 99.4% maximum applies to the reported 642-task V2 public set and may be near saturation; the 51-task Hard split is a separate cohort.
Do not compare V1 and V2 scores as if the task sets and protocols were identical.
entries.recommended_use: Replicate exact V2 revision, report public and Hard split separately, and add fresh repository-heldout tasks for generalization.

entries.title: Terminal-Bench 4.1 current leaderboard snapshot
methodology_facts: Terminal-Bench 4.0 release notes describe resource calibration, task fixes and removal of saturated tasks.
limitations: Leaderboard snapshot is time-sensitive and must be rechecked before a comparison.
Scores are system configurations, not model-only capability.
Do not infer cross-domain capability from terminal tasks.
entries.recommended_use: Pin the exact 4.1 task and harness revision; compare cost, tokens, wall time and system configuration, not only resolution rate.

entries.title: Epoch AI review of Terminal-Bench 4.0.0
limitations: The review concerns version 4.0.0 specifically.
Do not transfer the 30/66 finding automatically to later 4.1 tasks.
A noted scoring defect does not necessarily have equal severity across tasks.
entries.recommended_use: Re-audit the current benchmark revision and preserve task-level verifier defect reports.

entries.title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?
methodology_facts: Authors report that LIBERO and CALVIN fail multiple diagnostics, while RoboCasa and RoboTwin 2.0 fail fewer under their audit.
The audit includes a 0.09B probe without a language encoder that scores near reported SOTA on LIBERO.
limitations: This is a methodological audit, not a new physical-robot performance leaderboard.
Findings should be applied to exact benchmark versions and protocols; they do not imply every later benchmark release is invalid.
entries.recommended_use: Run shortcut probes, held-out data-source tests, within-distribution perturbations, adequate repeated trials and real-hardware transfer checks.

entries.title: AI data centres as grid-interactive assets

reported_metrics.qos: maintained under the study's declared AI quality-of-service guarantees

limitations: Result is specific to the studied Phoenix facility, cluster, workloads, controls and measurement boundary.
It is not a universal flexibility target and does not demonstrate every facility can defer the same share of demand.
Grid-facing power reduction must be separated from whole-facility energy per completed work and rebound.
entries.recommended_use: Treat as a field replication envelope; match hardware/workload/QoS/measurement and report whole-facility energy, rebound and opportunity cost.

entries.title: Supply Chain Traceability: A Manufacturing Meta-Framework
methodology_facts: Defines an industry-neutral meta-framework for organizing, linking and querying supply-chain traceability data across diverse ecosystems.
Emphasizes cryptographic links, interoperability, selective disclosure and continued use of existing standards.
limitations: This is a meta-framework/report, not product certification or a single mandatory API.
NIST's announced Python reference implementation was still undergoing final review at publication.
entries.recommended_use: Use as a mapping and design reference; test interoperability against independent existing standards implementations.

entries.title: GS1 EPCIS / CBV 2.0.1 normative artefacts
methodology_facts: Provides event semantics and normative JSON-LD context, REST/OpenAPI interfaces, query schema and JSON/JSON-LD validation artefacts.
limitations: Standards conformance is not performance superiority.
A local checkpoint or batch field cannot be mapped by name alone; identifier granularity, business step, disposition, time and quantity semantics must be explicit.
entries.recommended_use: Select a bounded event profile and round-trip through an independent EPCIS implementation.

entries.title: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 and Data Integrity 1.0
methodology_facts: Defines a machine-verifiable, privacy-respecting credential data model and cryptographic integrity mechanisms.
limitations: A credential does not establish that the underlying real-world statement is true.
Legacy JWT credential profiles must not be relabeled VC DM 2.0 / Data Integrity conformant without an explicit profile and tests.
entries.recommended_use: Pin the securing mechanism and profile; test issuer/subject binding, status, validity, disclosure and correlation.

entries.title: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains
methodology_facts: Standards-track architecture for single-issuer signed statement transparency.
limitations: RFC 9943 is a Proposed Standard.
Related SCITT APIs and CCF receipt-profile drafts remain in the publication pipeline and are not final RFCs as of 2026-11-13.
A local event hash or DKG claim ID is not a transparency receipt.
entries.recommended_use: Keep statement identity, issuer signature and independent transparency receipt as separate verified evidence.

admission_rules: Every result must pin task revision, task universe, harness, model/provider, tools, resource limits, grader and environment.
Rerun after task, environment, resource, tool access or agent execution semantics change.
Regrade after verifier/oracle/judge semantics change when exact run artifacts remain valid.
Reuse only after metadata/non-semantic changes with unchanged benchmark, environment and grader semantics.
Keep reported, independent-review, field-demonstration and normative-standard evidence classes separate.
Do not promote provider-reported results into independent reproduction.
No weighted aggregate can compensate for critical security, authority, evidence or physical-safety failure.
claim_limit: This register is a planning reference, not a Luminous benchmark result or a universal SOTA leaderboard.
